operator_io_quirks: All 16 tables report rows=0 and empty samples/storage: the frozen original is effectively empty (or unreadable), so original_values/original_sizes are all empty/0 and literal pool must come from TRAIN SQL only.
DDL uses backtick-quoted FK parents (`actor`("aid")) while tables are double-quoted; sqlite_master DDL must be replayed verbatim for the empty clone.

FK targets are non-unique parents: cast.msid, classification.msid, directed_by.msid, made_by.msid, tags.msid, written_by.msid all reference copyright(msid), which is NOT the PK (PK is id) and has no unique index -> dangling/duplicate parent values are legal.
written_by has NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must no-op and drop_unique_duplicates has nothing to drop.
writer.name and writer.nationality are declared INT but semantically text (names/nationalities) -> Number fuzzer will emit integers for name/nationality; storage class contradiction.
movie.budget and tv_series.budget are declared TEXT (money) -> String fuzzer, not Number.
release_year / birth_year / num_of_episodes / num_of_seasons are INT -> Number fuzzer, not Date/Year; no date-typed column anywhere.
All columns notnull=0, no CHECK, no UNIQUE, no DEFAULT -> nothing enforced in Python; only PK/insert errors skip rows.
Table names are lowercase, no spaces, no mixed case; identifiers still must be double-quoted per spec.
copyright is a hub: 6 child tables FK to it; its msid is the join key but not unique, so FK consistency draws from a non-unique parent column.
cast.role is INT (role id), not text role name -> Number fuzzer.
No self-references, no composite PKs, no missing-parent FKs in this DB.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer (scale from INT -> scale 0, range [-1,1] then perturb +-1/+-2) for all *_id, birth_year, release_year, num_of_*, role, and for writer.name/nationality (declared INT).
String fuzzer (length 20, charset a-zA-Z 0-9()) for gender, name, nationality, birth_city, title, title_aka, budget, genre, keyword, country_code, company.name.

FK columns (cast.aid/msid, classification.gid/msid, directed_by.did/msid, made_by.pid/msid, tags.kid/msid, written_by.wid/msid) draw from parent's final column with replacement; copyright.msid non-unique so many children share few msids.
Empty original -> original_values empty -> samplers rely on literal pool + fresh draws; p=0.2 default, whole-instance p=0 w.p. 0.3.
PKs are single-column INT -> max_l0=inf for PK columns, so fresh PK draws never reuse -> PKs unique, no duplicate-row drops expected.

Likely FN driver: implausible values (writer.name as integer, budget as random string, gender as random charset) make gold predicates like name LIKE '%X%' or budget comparisons trivially empty/over-full.
Likely FP driver: copyright.msid non-unique means joins produce many-to-many blowups; TS does not model that ties exist, so COUNT/DISTINCT queries may match by accident.
No date columns -> Date fuzzer never used; no Bool/Bit/Time columns.
written_by has no PK -> no dedup, duplicate (msid,wid) rows possible, inflating join cardinalities.
release_year as Number in [-1,1]+perturb -> years like 0,1,-1,2, not 1990s; year-range predicates (release_year > 2000) return empty in TS but non-empty in real data -> FN.
budget TEXT random strings -> numeric budget comparisons (CAST) behave erratically.
